# National Geographic

> > National Geographic's exploration and science journalism covering wildlife photography, space discoveries, archaeology, and environmental stories from around the world.

This collection showcases National Geographic's adventure and science reporting, featuring work from renowned photographers like Steve Winter and Frans Lanting, alongside coverage of major discoveries from NASA, archaeological expeditions, and natural phenomena. The content spans wildlife documentation in locations like Brazil's Pantanal and Botswana, to exoplanet discoveries and ancient civilizations.

## Key Topics

- Wildlife Photography
- Space Exploration & Exoplanets
- NASA Missions
- Archaeological Discoveries
- Climate & Environmental Change
- Natural Phenomena
- Ancient Civilizations
- Solar System Science
- Conservation Photography
- Hubble Space Telescope
- Kuiper Belt & Dwarf Planets
- Historical Expeditions
- Marine Biology
- Olympic Science

## Space & Astronomy

- [Hubble Telescope at 20: NASA Astronomers' Top Photos](https://www.nationalgeographic.com/adventure/article/100424-hubble-telescope-20th-anniversary-pictures): NASA astronomers select top Hubble Space Telescope photos for 20th anniversary
- [Our Solar System May Have Millions of Twins](https://www.nationalgeographic.com/adventure/article/100108-solar-systems-like-ours-twins): Survey finds Jupiter-Saturn systems suggest habitable Earth-like planets
- [New Planet System May Be Most Populated Yet Found](https://www.nationalgeographic.com/adventure/article/101130-new-planets-found-solar-system-twin-science-space): HD 10180 system discovered with Neptune-like planets resembling solar system
- [Three New "Plutos"? Possible Dwarf Planets Found](https://www.nationalgeographic.com/adventure/article/110811-three-new-dwarf-planets-pluto-kuiper-belt-space-science): Three potential dwarf planets discovered in Kuiper belt near Pluto
- ["Suicide" Comet Storm Hits Sun—Bigger Sun-Kisser Coming?](https://www.nationalgeographic.com/adventure/article/110117-comets-storm-sun-soho-nasa-sungrazing-science-space): SOHO captures sungrazing comet swarm possibly heralding larger visitor

## Archaeological Discoveries

- [100th Anniversary of Roald Amundsen Reaching South Pole—How the Grueling Race Was Won](https://www.nationalgeographic.com/adventure/article/100th-anniversary-of-norwegian-roald-amundsen-reaching-south-polefind-out-how-the-grueling-race-was): Roald Amundsen's 100th anniversary of winning South Pole race vs Scott
- [Pictures: Odd Maya Tomb Yields Jeweled Teeth, More](https://www.nationalgeographic.com/adventure/article/100721-maya-tomb-human-fingers-king-guatemala-science-pictures): Maya royal tomb at El Zotz, Guatemala reveals jeweled teeth and sacrifices
- [Jacques Cousteau Centennial: What He Did, Why He Matters](https://www.nationalgeographic.com/adventure/article/100611-jacques-cousteau-100th-anniversary-birthday-legacy-google): Jacques Cousteau's centennial celebrates aqua-lung invention and legacy
- [Pocahontas's Wedding Chapel Found at Jamestown](https://www.nationalgeographic.com/adventure/article/101110-pocahontas-wedding-chapel-jamestown-science): Archaeologists discover Pocahontas and John Rolfe's wedding church ruins
- [Pictures: Pagan-Cult Worship Objects Found](https://www.nationalgeographic.com/adventure/article/100616-israel-pagan-cult-tomb-objects-pictures): Bronze Age pagan cult artifacts discovered at Tel Qashish, Israel
- [Ancient Popcorn Found—Made 2,000 Years Earlier Than Thought in Peru](https://www.nationalgeographic.com/adventure/article/120119-national-popcorn-day-corn-peru-archaeology-food-science): Peru archaeology reveals popcorn eaten 2,000 years earlier than believed

## Natural Phenomena & Earth Sciences

- [Video: Giant Undersea Volcano Revealed](https://www.nationalgeographic.com/adventure/article/100714-indonesia-okeanos-volcano-exploration-vin-video): First footage of 10,000-foot underwater volcano Kawio Barat, Indonesia
- [Vancouver 2010 to Be Warmest Winter Olympics Yet](https://www.nationalgeographic.com/adventure/article/100212-vancouver-2010-warmest-winter-olympics): Vancouver 2010 Winter Olympics faces warmest temperatures on record
- [Did Olympic Athletes Peak in the 1980s?](https://www.nationalgeographic.com/adventure/article/100226-vancouver-2010-olympics-new-world-record): Study finds Olympic performance nearing human limits since 1980s

## Photo Highlights & Editors' Picks

- [Our Favorite Instagram Photos: Jaguar Cubs and Penguin Chicks](https://www.nationalgeographic.com/adventure/article/0909-favorite-instagram): Weekly Instagram photo highlights featuring jaguars in Brazil's Pantanal
- [Pictures We Love: Best of October](https://www.nationalgeographic.com/adventure/article/111031-best-news-pictures-lightning-volcano-beluga-bubble): October 2011 editors' picks: volcanic lightning, beluga bubbles, more
- [Pictures We Love: Best of December](https://www.nationalgeographic.com/adventure/article/111229-best-pictures-month-auroras-deserts-rivers-refugees): December 2011 photo highlights: winter swimmers, Egyptian treasures
